page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth tests, including read-only small block, read-only large block, and write large block operations. Multi-threaded performance is highly competitive, as evidenced by top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation with Clang, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression.

The m8gb.16xlarge is highly optimized for memory-bound and multi-threaded workloads. It excels in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving, all of which recorded top-tier benchmark performance. For machine learning tasks, the instance exhibits a performance tradeoff: while text generation using medium and large LLM models is strong, text generation for smaller models is weak, and prompt processing speeds across all model sizes remain average. This profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for high-density multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, and high-throughput web serving, while being less suited for single-threaded tasks or local-storage-dependent databases.
